condition: Blunt polytrauma with haemorrhagic shock (ATLS class III)
summary: 34-year-old motorcyclist hit by a car 40 min ago: GCS 13, RR 30, SpO₂ 92 % on oxygen, BP 88/50, HR 132, positive FAST (LUQ and Morison's pouch), pelvic tenderness, base deficit −8, lactate 5.2.

inputs.hpi: Motorcyclist, estimated 60 km/h, struck by a car 40 minutes ago and thrown several metres. Helmet on. Brief loss of consciousness at scene per paramedics. Complains of left-sided chest, abdominal and pelvic pain.

exam.general: Pale, clammy, GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6), confused. HR 132, BP 88/50, RR 30, SpO2 92% on 15 L. Capillary refill 4 s. Haemodynamically unstable.
exam.respiratory: Left chest wall tenderness, reduced air entry left base. Trachea central.
exam.abdomen: Distended, tender with guarding in the left upper quadrant. Pelvis tender on gentle palpation (not sprung).
exam.neuro: Moves all four limbs. Pupils equal and reactive.

imaging.name: FAST scan
imaging.result: Free fluid in the splenorenal recess and Morison's pouch. Pericardium clear.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Blunt abdominal trauma with haemoperitoneum and haemorrhagic shock (ATLS class III)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Blunt polytrauma with haemorrhagic shock (ATLS class III), positive FAST, suspected splenic injury and pelvic injury. Primary survey, haemorrhage control, blood products, damage-control laparotomy.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — initial assessment and management
guideline.section: Chapter 1: primary survey in order — control of exsanguinating external haemorrhage, airway with cervical spine restriction, breathing, circulation with haemorrhage control, disability, exposure (x/c-ABCDE); adjuncts (FAST, CXR, pelvic XR); resuscitation before definitive imaging in unstable patients
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 1.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — shock
guideline.section: Chapter 3, Table 3-1: haemorrhage classes I (<15%), II (15–30%), III (31–40%), IV (>40%) with heart rate, blood pressure, pulse pressure, respiratory rate, urine output, GCS and base deficit; class III–IV need blood products / massive transfusion protocol; early haemorrhage control; minimise crystalloid; beta-blockers and age blunt the tachycardic response
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 3.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — abdominal and pelvic trauma
guideline.section: Chapter 5: FAST in the unstable patient; haemodynamically abnormal patient with positive FAST → laparotomy; CT only in stable patients; evisceration, peritonitis or haemodynamic instability after penetrating trauma → laparotomy; selective non-operative management of anterior stab wounds in stable patients
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 5.

guideline.name: CRASH-2 — tranexamic acid in bleeding trauma patients
guideline.section: Tranexamic acid 1 g over 10 min then 1 g over 8 h, given within 3 h of injury; no benefit and possible harm when started after 3 h
guideline.citation: CRASH-2 collaborators. The importance of early treatment with tranexamic acid in bleeding trauma patients: an exploratory analysis of the CRASH-2 randomised controlled trial. Lancet. 2011;377:1096–101.

guideline.name: NICE NG39 — Major trauma: assessment and initial management
guideline.section: Pre-hospital/hospital: tranexamic acid as soon as possible in major haemorrhage; pelvic binder for suspected pelvic haemorrhage; ratio-based blood product resuscitation; restrictive crystalloid; whole-body CT for suspected multiple injuries once stable enough
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Major trauma: assessment and initial management (NG39). London: NICE; 2016.

rationale: Base trauma case: high-energy blunt mechanism with ATLS class III haemorrhagic shock (tachycardia, hypotension, tachypnoea, confusion, base deficit −8) and a positive FAST. Tests primary-survey ordering, shock recognition, blood products, laparotomy for FAST-positive instability, TXA within 3 h and pelvic binder. ICD S39.91XA (unspecified injury of abdomen).
